answer.verdict: Fight non-GS game-thread time is host per-packet copying plus a timer poll on every guest call: GifArbiter heap-copies every GIF packet, MFIFO copies the same qwords again and processVIF1Data RMW-unpacks them, and accountCycles runs EE+idle IOP timers on every dispatch and loop back-edge. Visible VU1 blocks are the transform at pc 0x2e30 and the clip block at 0x2110, not recompiled EE functions.

facts.c: Profile window TEKKEN4_PROFILE=88:12, TEKKEN4_PROFILE_THREADS=all, PS2X_GS_DRAIN_STATS=1. 4786 game-thread samples. 18*4786=86148 matches the other-thread sample count, so every tick suspended the game thread and 18 others. Sampler sleeps 1ms then does that work; 12000/4786=2.51ms between game-thread samples.

During seconds 88-99 the log is 21,20,15,18 then 20 fps eight times, then 19 fps. GS primitives/s in that window run from 512275 (s88) to 696129 (s96) and 689043 (s98). NtWaitForAlertByThreadId 22.6% plus WaitForWorkersUnlocked 2.9% leaves ~74.5% of game-thread samples outside those two waits.

Fight VIF1 path is MFIFO: fromSPR copies SPR to the ring 16 bytes at a time, markModified per qword, then drainMfifo. drainMfifo builds std::vector out by insert of 16 bytes per qword (realloc = RtlAllocateHeap + memmove) and calls processVIF1Data on that copy.

processVIF1Data UNPACK (opcode&0x60)==0x60 always read-modify-writes each vector: memcpy 16 from VU mem, per-component memcpy from the stream, 4-lane mask/mode loop, memcpy 16 back. Constant sizes are inlinable, so that cost sits in the 7.1% processVIF1Data symbol. A carry std::vector is only when a command spans DMA slices.

Every GIF packet, including each XGKICK, goes through GifArbiter::submit: pkt.data.resize(sizeBytes) then memcpy of the whole packet, then push_back. submitGifPacket defaults drainImmediately=true, so drain() runs at once and the copy is not a queue. finishXgkick calls submitGifPacket(Path1) with that default.

UploadImage's copies are 8-byte memcpy inside that function (own symbol 2.9%). A full-frame present copy is once per vsync. The outlined memcpy symbol is the runtime-size copies: GifArbiter::submit and vector growth, plus the fromSPR 16-byte loop if the compiler did not inline it. Flat samples cannot split those callers.

advanceEeTimers runs from EeScheduler::accountCycles on every checkpointDue. dispatchGuestBranch charges kGuestDispatchCycles=8; a generated backward edge calls eeCheckpointDue() which defaults to kGeneratedCheckpointCycles=32. Each call does unordered_map find of GIF_STAT 0x10003020 and clears FQC, then up to 4 timers with 64-bit div/mod by kEeClockHz 294912000.
facts.ref: EeScheduler.cpp:357-400; ps2_runtime.cpp:1364-1367; control_flow_emitter.cpp:178-183; ee_scheduler.h:267-268; ps2_memory.cpp:163,408-435; ps2_memory.h:382,461

facts.c: GIF_STAT read keeps stored FQC (only low 4 bits are rebuilt). processPendingTransfers sets FQC and does not clear it after the synchronous transfer. The clear is the advanceEeTimers map update. Deleting that update without clearing FQC at transfer end leaves FQC set.

accountCycles also calls advanceIopEeCycles. runEeCycles divides by 8, so an 8-cycle dispatch is runCycles(1). The idle path in runCycles jumps to nextWake but clamps to target, so a 1-cycle request never jumps. serviceDue scans 6 timers, nextEventCycle scans them again. No IOP guest CPU symbol is in the top 30, so the fight path is the idle poll (sound RPC is the silent HLE).

FLUSHE/FLUSH/FLUSHA in processVIF1Data are empty continues. VU1 MSCAL calls VU1Interpreter::execute which always resetScheduler() then run(). resetScheduler value-inits the pipeline arrays (m_vfReady 32*4 uint64, m_vfLatestWrite the same, flag/store/vf/vi/acc queues) and m_xgkick.reset(), which does not zero the 64KB XGKICK packet.

Direct register writes are on (status: setDirectRegisterWrites(true)). Native runNative does not consult m_vfReady. resetScheduler still wipes those arrays on every MSCAL. Skipping the wipe is wrong if an interpreter miss follows an in-flight FDIV, because FLUSHE does not wait.

b2e30_ec9e8390, b2110_101d0300, b1620_b38895a7, b1598_5e893185 are generated native VU1 blocks, not EE functions. b2e30 pc 0x2e30, 51 pairs, no flag tail, key 0xfe7cb42cec9e8390: matrix MADDs, DIV, SQ to VU mem, ends on a vi compare. b2110 pc 0x2110, 45 pairs, no tail: CLIP, FTOI, XGKICK-class callLower, matrix. b1620 pc 0x1620, 14 pairs, has tail. b1598 pc 0x1598, 11 pairs, has tail. Longer blocks exist (63, 58, 57 pairs) and are under the 0.5% cutoff, so the fight runs 0x2e30 and 0x2110 more.

b2e30 pair 0 is VU1NativeAccess::callLower of lower 0x81c04f3f (op 0x40, special the generator marks calls_out). execLower is absent from the top 30, so the callout body is under 0.5%. macVal/clamp temps for flags that only q44 consumes are inline and pure; MSVC can DCE them. That DCE was not checked in the binary.

runNative per block: slot lookup, optional blockTiming, the native fn, finishBlockTiming, commitReadyPipelines if the cycle passed m_nextCommitCycle. CSR is switched once per run, not per block. 1.7% is this dispatcher; the block bodies are the b* symbols.

MSVC std::mutex locks are Mtx_lock + SRW release (RtlReleaseSRWLockExclusive 0.8% with Mtx_lock 1.5%). Submit takes std::mutex m_mutex once per primitive. GS::processGIFPacket takes std::recursive_mutex m_stateMutex once per packet. queueCompletedDmacCause takes m_completedDmacMutex and push_back on every DMA completion, including each fromSPR. Pad locks are per read. Which lock is the 2.3% is not in the flat profile; per-primitive Submit matches the rate better than per-frame pad.
GS debug history is paused by default, so recordDrawDebugEventUnlocked returns before the per-primitive history store.

The symbol memchr is host CRT. The guest stub ps2_stubs::memchr is a per-byte loop via getConstMemPtr and does not call ::memchr. No other memchr( in ps2xRuntime or ps2xIOP sources. STL char_traits::find / string::find call CRT memchr. 0.7% has no proven hot caller.

Sampler stores only Rip (CONTEXT_CONTROL) and names it with SymFromAddr after the window. It inserts into unordered_map while the target is still suspended. A stack walk that allocates then can deadlock on the heap lock the game thread holds inside RtlAllocateHeap.

fix.change: When drainImmediately is true (the default, and the XGKICK/DIRECT path), call the GS process function on the caller's bytes. Do not resize+memcpy+push_back+stable_sort a one-packet queue. Keep the queue only for a real PATH3-vs-DIRECTHL overlap. Expected ~4-6% of the game thread (the bulk of memcpy 5.9% and a large share of RtlAllocateHeap 3.3%). Risk: the caller must keep the bytes alive through processGIFPacket; drainMfifo's vector and the XGKICK packet already do. Do not also count this percent in the gs-throughput raster changes.

Fast path before the per-vector RMW: mask off, mode 0 or 3, cl>=wl, 32-bit components. If wl==cl==1, one memcpy of writeVectorCount*16 into VU mem at vuAddr (wrapping at 0x400). Other cl: one 16-byte store per vector, no load of the old qword and no per-lane loop. Leave masking, STMOD 1/2, wl>cl fill, and sub-32-bit formats on the existing loop. Expected ~4-6% of the game thread out of processVIF1Data 7.1%, less if the fight's UNPACKs are masked or 16-bit. Risk: VIF write-protect and row-fill must stay off this path; add a unit test per vn/vl that the slow path already covers.

fromSPR: memcpy each contiguous ring span, markModified once per span (the ring at 0x100000 does not overlap the code region 0x180080). drainMfifo: drop std::vector out; walk tags in the ring and pass each span to processVIF1Data, carrying a partial command across the wrap as today. Expected ~2-4% more of memcpy/memmove/RtlAllocateHeap after the GIF fix (memmove 1.1% is mostly this realloc). Sum of this fix plus the GIF fix should stay under the 10.3% those three CRT symbols add to. Risk: a tag whose data wraps the ring, and TTE's tag-hi qword, must still reach VIF in order.

Accumulate EE cycles. Call advanceEeTimers only when m_eeCycle reaches cyclesUntilNextEeTimerInterrupt (already at ps2_memory.cpp:484). Clear GIF_STAT.FQC at the end of processPendingTransfers and drainMfifo, and delete the unordered_map find from advanceEeTimers. Call runEeCycles with the accumulated batch (a few thousand EE cycles, and always on SIF/RPC/vsync and on a GIF_STAT or SIF register read), so idle runCycles can jump to nextWake once per batch instead of runCycles(1) per guest call. Expected ~4% (2.5+0.8+0.6+0.6). Risk: a guest that polls FQC or an IOP flag must hit a flush on that read; a batch with no flush spins. Future IOP sound needs the same flush on the RPC path. Do not batch across an EE read of an IOP-owned register.

gs-throughput owns this. Submit's std::mutex is once per primitive on a lock-free queue. Take it only for WaitForWorkers, uploads, and CLUT, not for the enqueue. Expected ~1.5-2.3% including RtlReleaseSRWLockExclusive, if stacks show this mutex rather than m_stateMutex or m_completedDmacMutex. Risk: workers that read m_queuedWritePages or m_clut without the lock. Do not add this percent on top of a gs-throughput patch that already drops the lock.

When the previous execute() stayed in runNative and no FDIV/EFU/store is in flight, skip the array value-inits. One memset of the POD pipeline block if a wipe is still required. Do not touch the 64KB XGKICK buffer. Expected ~0.5-0.8%. Risk: FLUSHE is a no-op, so a miss on the next program can observe a future ready-cycle if the wipe is skipped while m_fdiv.valid or a pending mask is set. Gate the skip on those flags.

After the GIF, VIF, and timer fixes. Optional: have a block return its successor fn so runNative is not entered per short block. Expected up to ~1% of the 1.7% dispatcher, and it does not shrink b2e30 (1.1%) or b2110 (0.8%), which are the transform and clip bodies. Risk: budget, E-bit, and interpreter-miss returns must still break out. Not worth it before the copies and the timer poll.

contra: Prompt called b2e30_ec9e8390 and b2110_101d0300 likely recompiled EE functions. They are vu1n blocks (vu1n_part2.cpp:1934, vu1n_part0.cpp:1966).
Seconds 90 and 91 inside the 88:12 window are 15 and 18 fps (stdout.txt:320-323), so the sample is not a pure 19-21 fps slice.

memcpy 5.9%, RtlAllocateHeap 3.3%, and memmove 1.1% have several callers. The GIF-vs-MFIFO split in fix[0] and fix[2] is from call shape, not from stacks. Adding both expected percents can overshoot 10.3%.
Mtx_lock 1.5% is attributed to GSCpuBackend::Submit by rate. processGIFPacket's recursive_mutex and queueCompletedDmacCause's mutex are other Mtx_lock callers. Stacks can move that 2%.
Dead macVal temps in b2e30 are unused after q44 (vu1n_part2.cpp:1890). If the compiler already dropped them, a generator change saves nothing.

Clearing GIF_STAT.FQC only inside advanceEeTimers is what makes a synchronous DMA look finished. A timer batch that leaves the find in place, or removes it without an end-of-transfer clear, changes the poll the game sees.
No per-frame counts of fromSPR, XGKICK, or UNPACK vn/vl were measured. 25k-35k GS primitives/frame is primitives/s divided by fps from stdout.txt:316-337, and one primitive is not one packet.
checks: RtlVirtualUnwind stack samples of memcpy, RtlAllocateHeap, memmove, Mtx_lock, memchr on the same 88:12 fight window.
A counter, not a new profile: UNPACK vn/vl/mask/mode/cl/wl, fromSPR qwc, XGKICK bytes, GifArbiter::submit calls, checkpointDue calls, per frame.
After the FQC move: a GIF_STAT spin in a test must see FQC 0 once processPendingTransfers returns, and the existing VIF/MFIFO tests still pass.
GOW_VU1N_VERIFY on the UNPACK fast path and on a resetScheduler skip, including a program that MSCALS with an FDIV still in flight.
open: Caller of CRT memchr (0.7%). Stub does not call it. STL string::find or some other host code. Stacks settle it. No fix ranked.
Share of processVIF1Data that is V4-32 with STCYCL 0x0101 versus masked or 16-bit UNPACK. Fast-path percent moves with that mix.
How many fromSPR and XGKICK packets the fight submits per frame. Decides GIF copy vs MFIFO vector vs fromSPR loop.
Whether the shipped binary DCE'd b2e30's unused macVal/q temps.
IOP batch size once a real sound IRX is on this thread. The fight profile is the idle poll only.
Hidden native blocks under the 0.5% cutoff. Their sum can exceed the four named blocks (3.1%). A stack or a per-block counter is the way to add them.

GS wait stays ~22.6%+2.9%. These cuts are game-thread percents. They do not add to an fps target with the gs-throughput work, and the close camera (status) inflates the primitive rate this window measured.
